correctness.rationale: The 2-channel half-density Zak identity is fixed by normalization and direct calculation; the entire frame spectrum is the continuous fiber-energy range. Parity gives product or affine-in-t exact expression, yielding globally sharp bounds and exhaustive equality cases. Completeness at nonframe parameters follows from measure-zero energy zero sets. The unique optimum and perturbation normal forms follow from strict trigonometric-sign and Taylor arguments, not sampling. The 3,536 standalone finite checks are confirmatory only.

originality.rationale: The new statement is a sharp all-complex-coefficient, all-integer-delay classification and conditioning theorem for the sum of two translates of the order-two hat as one analysis generator, not a restatement of the basic Zak criterion or of pure-spline frame-set results. Comparison of theorem hypotheses and conclusions in arXiv:2609.00481v1, arXiv:2609.13116v1 and arXiv:1708.04803v1 shows that those do not claim the parity-dependent two-pulse filtered spectrum, completeness at singularities, global design optimum or quadratic-versus-quartic phase unfolding. Published indexed summaries describe nearby but distinct questions. Novelty may still be limited by older finite-impulse-response filtered-window work.
residual_risks: Older Gabor/filter-bank theory may encode the same parameter family under a polyphase or FIR-filter formulation.
Published indexed close papers were compared by abstracts; their repository full texts could not be read and are not claimed to be ruled out.
No independent novelty or mathematical audit has been conducted.

value.rationale: The complete spectrum for every integer pulse delay and complex coherent amplitude has direct reconstruction-stability meaning, including exact failure loci, completeness versus stable frames, globally unique conditioning-optimal geometry and different singular unfolding orders. These nontrivial uniform parameter and boundary features are not routine numerical samples or a single special value; the formula provides a reproducible finite trigonometric optimization for every odd delay.
